executive_summary.title: Executive Summary
executive_summary.content: Monolithic two-terminal perovskite-silicon tandem solar cells have achieved significant milestones with certified power conversion efficiencies reaching 33.9% [cite_exec_1]. However, their performance can be constrained by operational degradation mechanisms, notably light-induced halide segregation in mixed iodide-bromide perovskites [cite_exec_3]. Advanced encapsulation architectures utilizing double-barrier layers have shown considerable promise in mitigating moisture ingress during accelerated damp-heat testing [cite_exec_2].

sections.title: Degradation Mechanisms and Environmental Stress Testing
sections.content: Under continuous 1-sun illumination, mixed iodide-bromide perovskites suffer from light-induced halide segregation [cite_cite_1]. This segregation leads to the formation of low-bandgap iodide-rich clusters that function as non-radiative recombination centers, ultimately reducing the open-circuit voltage by up to 140 mV [cite_cite_1]. In addition to illumination stressors, environmental moisture poses a severe risk to device stability. Encapsulating tandems with double-barrier layers consisting of 20 nm atomic-layer-deposited tin oxide (SnO2) capped with polyisobutylene (PIB) edge seals completely blocks moisture ingress [cite_cite_2]. Consequently, devices subjected to IEC 61215 damp-heat testing at 85 degrees Celsius and 85% relative humidity successfully retained 95% of their initial efficiency after 1,500 hours of continuous accelerated stress [cite_cite_3].

conclusion.title: Conclusion and Future Outlook
conclusion.content: Addressing degradation mechanisms in perovskite-silicon tandem solar cells requires focusing on intrinsic material stability and robust external encapsulation. Light-induced halide segregation forms low-bandgap iodide-rich clusters that act as non-radiative recombination centers and reduce open-circuit voltage [cite_conc_1], while advanced barrier technologies such as ALD SnO2 combined with PIB edge seals offer an effective defense against environmental moisture [cite_conc_2]. Overcoming these stressors is critical for scaling tandem photovoltaics toward commercial viability.

limitations: The scope is limited to data concerning mixed iodide-bromide perovskites and specific double-barrier encapsulation methods.
Long-term field data beyond 1,500 hours of accelerated damp-heat testing are not yet captured in the current source context.
